headline: High risk of prompt/data leakage and cascading errors: Open Interpreter’s filesystem/clipboard/code execution can feed Plane’s task content, while Plane’s broad networked task surfaces can amplify mistakes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the local filesystem and clipboard, and its state is shared via filesystem; Plane accepts files, notes, hyperlinks, and issue content. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled task text or files from Plane can be copied into Open Interpreter and treated as instructions. Plane is not shown to sanitize provenance, so the interaction is not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or files without provenance labels, injection is possible.
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced confirmation, malicious instructions in Plane artifacts can execute.
mitigations: Keep Plane and Open Interpreter on separate workspaces.
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter.
Require manual review before copying Plane text into Open Interpreter.
Strip instructions from imported notes/files before use.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between task content and executable prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can send data to configured model providers; Plane stores files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks. If the same local workspace or copied files are used, sensitive local data can flow from Open Interpreter into Plane artifacts or from Plane uploads into Open Interpreter prompts. The profiles do not show isolation or DLP by default.
conditions: IF a local file containing secrets is opened by Open Interpreter and then attached to Plane, leakage occurs.
IF Open Interpreter forwards copied Plane content to a third-party model provider, Plane data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the shared workspace.
Use separate directories for Plane uploads and Open Interpreter inputs.
Review copied content before sending it to model providers.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if they were handled locally.
requires-engineering: enforce redaction/DLP on shared files and clipboard.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write, shell, and git mutation; Plane has no write_filesystem capability and is not shown to modify git or local files. The pair therefore has limited direct write-write conflict, though Open Interpreter can still overwrite shared files that Plane reads. Because only one side writes locally, the conflict is present but narrower than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory, Open Interpreter can overwrite files Plane expects to remain stable.
IF Plane exports artifacts into a shared folder, Open Interpreter may modify them concurrently.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid sharing git working trees between the agents.
Lock shared files before Open Interpreter edits them.
Export Plane artifacts as read-only copies.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; Plane can store issues, tasks, and notes that may be treated as authoritative work items. If Plane content is fed into Open Interpreter without verification, or Open Interpreter outputs are pasted back into Plane as tasks, errors can cascade across multiple work products. Neither profile shows a built-in verification gate.
conditions: IF Plane issues or notes are used as authoritative prompts for Open Interpreter, mistakes can propagate into code or shell actions.
IF Open Interpreter outputs are copied into Plane tasks without human verification, downstream work items inherit errors.
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on Open Interpreter output.
Mark Plane items derived from AI output as untrusted.
Use a checklist for code or shell actions generated by Open Interpreter.
Keep a separate review queue for AI-sourced tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated validation before syncing outputs into Plane.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency or certification constraints. The main compliance concern is operational: Open Interpreter can touch local files and model-provider APIs, while Plane stores issues, files, and notes. No explicit mismatch is documented, so only a low residual compliance risk is visible from the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane and then processed by Open Interpreter through a non-approved model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not present in either profile, the pair may violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Use only approved model providers with Open Interpreter.
Review retention settings in Plane before storing sensitive items.
Document the data flow for any regulated workload.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review for regulated data paths.
